name: apply_patch
description: Apply localized file edits using `*** Replace in line:`, a `*** Begin Patch` envelope, or a unified diff. Prefer the smallest format that fits; use patch_file for large patches.

file_path.description: Absolute target path for a single-file unified diff. Optional when the patch carries a git-style header or a `*** Update File:` envelope (the path is read from the patch). Ignored for `*** Begin Patch` envelopes. `path` is accepted as an alias.

patch.description:
The edit to apply. Prefer the smallest format that fits:

(A) One substring on one uniquely identifiable line:
```
*** Begin Patch
*** Replace in line: <absolute/path>
anchor: <substring that uniquely identifies the target line>
old: <exact substring on that line to replace>
new: <replacement substring>
*** End Patch
```

(B) Larger edits, multiple files, additions, or deletions:
```
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: <absolute/path>
@@
 <unchanged context line>
-<line to remove>
+<line to add>
 <unchanged context line>
*** End Patch
```
Use `*** Add File: <path>` with `+`-prefixed content and `*** Delete File: <path>` with no body. Repeat sections for multiple files.

(C) Plain unified diff: single-file diffs need `file_path` or `---` / `+++` headers; multi-file diffs (git-style `diff --git` headers or `---`/`+++` pairs) are split and applied per file automatically. It cannot delete files.

Copy file text exactly, but omit `read_file`'s `<number>\t` prefix. Context and removed lines must match the current file, including indentation. Do not use Markdown fences, mix formats, or send a zero-change patch.

Size guidance: the inline `patch` text is hard-capped at 8000 characters (the tool rejects anything larger); `patch_file` supports up to 64000 characters. Large patches may also be truncated by the context manager before reaching this tool. For large edits, split into multiple apply_patch calls (each with a few hunks). Batch multiple hunks in one call only when each hunk has uniquely identifiable context; for structurally similar blocks (e.g. repeated closures), apply one patch per block.

patch_file.description: Optional absolute path to a file containing the patch text (alternative to `patch`). Use for large patches: write the patch to a temp file with write_file(temp=true) (which registers it in the session temp registry), then pass its path here. The file must be a session temp file or inside the current working directory. Pass either `patch` or `patch_file`, not both.
